topic: Side planks for a stronger trunk

slides.headline: Side planks: tough, but worth it
slides.sub: A trunk exercise that works your hips too. How to build it.

slides.title: Why go sideways?
slides.body: Side planks load the muscles along the side of your trunk and hip together. These help you carry shopping on one side, change direction in sport and stay steady on one leg.

slides.title: Start on your knees
slides.body: Lie on your side, elbow under shoulder, knees bent. Lift your hips so you're straight from knees to head. Hold 10 to 20 seconds, 3 times each side, breathing normally.

slides.title: Then build up gradually
slides.body: When knee holds feel easy, straighten your legs, staggering your feet for balance. Add time before adding difficulty. Hip dips or a top-leg lift come later, once holds feel steady.

slides.title: Common slips to watch
slides.body: Hips sagging or piking back, the shoulder creeping up to your ear, and holding your breath. A mirror or quick phone video helps. Shorter, cleaner holds usually beat long wobbly ones.

slides.title: When to change it up
slides.body: If your shoulder grumbles, try a version with your hand on a bench. Sharp back pain, or pain spreading into a leg, is worth getting assessed before pushing on.

slides.headline: Want a trunk plan that fits you?

caption:
Side planks are hard. They're also one of the more useful trunk exercises you can do.

They load the side of your trunk and your hip at the same time, which helps with carrying things on one side, changing direction in sport and balancing on one leg. Handy with winter preseason starting.

Start on your knees, elbow under shoulder, and hold 10 to 20 seconds, 3 times a side. When that feels easy, straighten your legs. Add time before difficulty, and keep holds clean rather than long.

A grumbly shoulder usually just needs a different version. Sharp back pain or pain into a leg is worth getting checked.
